correctness.rationale: Independent exact recount confirms the witness: 12 distinct integer points, all 220 orientation determinants nonzero so general position holds and no vertex lies on a non-incident edge. Total edge pairs C(35,2)=595, disjoint pairs 420=C(5,2)*C(7,2)*2, quads 210 each with at most one crossing. Orientation-sign recount gives exactly 36 crossing disjoint pairs, matching crossing_list.csv (36 rows) and rotation_K57_36.json num_crossings 36; independent rational-parametric Fraction recount also gives 36; Fraction intersection computation gives 36 distinct interior points so no triple concurrency and no counting ambiguity. Rotation recomputed by atan2 matches stored rotation; stored crossing set matches recount as normalized edge pairs. Zarankiewicz arithmetic Z(5,7)=floor(5/2)*floor(4/2)*floor(7/2)*floor(6/2)=2*2*3*3=36 verified. Lower bound bar-cr>=cr holds because every rectilinear drawing is a topological drawing; cr(K(5,7))>=36 is cited from Kleitman 1970 (Crossref confirms title The crossing number of K5,n, 139 citations) and draft explicitly does not re-prove it. Kuratowski control (350 induced K3,3 each 6v/9e violating bipartite Euler e<=2v-4=8) correctly proves only nonplanarity, and draft explicitly states full cr>=36 is cited not proved by script, so no overclaim. Hashes of all six files match DRAFT. Quad-type audit confirms 36 convex non-alternating quads (exactly the crossing quads), 42 convex alternating, 132 non-convex. Proof (exact integer arithmetic plus cited theorem) is distinguished from experimental search (random plus annealing, ephemeral, not part of certificate). No essential inference, boundary condition, or computation fails.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval across Crossref and DataCite plus direct inspection of arXiv and publisher DOI pages shows nearest priors are different variants that do not give general-position rectilinear K(5,7) coordinates or value. Kleitman 1970 settles only topological cr=Z=36, not rectilinear. Nafar arXiv:2310.15882 restricts to double-circular arrangement on two concentric circles with radii-ratio optimization, not arbitrary general-position sets. Feder-Garber arXiv:1008.2638 defines Orchard crossing (line-separation) for K(n,n) only, different definition. Abrego et al. doi:10.1007/s00373-019-02076-5 is bipartite-cylindrical (vertices on cylinders), different topology. Fabila-Monroy-Lopez doi:10.7155/jgaa.00328 searches small point sets for complete graphs Kn, not bipartite 5+7 split. No retrieved source gives bar-cr(K(5,7))=36, general-position 12-point integer witness, or matching lower-bound certificate. Coordinates appear random-structured, not a standard 2-layer drawing (which would give 210 crossings), supporting non-triviality. Priority rests on substantive comparison of retrieved sources, not on timestamp or failed search alone.

value.rationale: Result closes an exact rectilinear value: bar-cr(K(5,7))=36 equals the topological optimum, with explicit integer point set in [0,40]^2, two independent exact verifiers, distinctness certificate, and rotation-system control, all replayable in seconds with stdlib Python. This is independently worth finding later as a citable benchmark for graph-drawing and VLSI tables. It is not a textbook restatement (topological 36 is textbook via Kleitman; rectilinear equality is new content and draft claims originality only for the upper-bound witness). It is not mere parameter substitution (K(5,7) is presented as smallest open stratum in K(5,7-9) band; naive 2-layer gives 210, so 36 is non-trivial; method is random search plus annealing with exact orientation counting, observed to reach Z for neighboring strata but only K(5,7) certified, with conjecture stated as uncertified). It is not a tiny unmotivated gain (open to closed exact value, not epsilon improvement; fallback interval not needed because bound is tight). It is not an unexplained enumeration (single witness with full verification log, quad-type breakdown, distinct-point check, and honest limitations; no order-type enumeration claimed). Deviation from planned rotation/B&B lower bound is intentional and documented because topological bound is already tight.

residual_risks: Lower bound depends on external Kleitman 1970 theorem cited without re-proof; audit verified citation metadata and arithmetic but did not re-verify the 1970 proof itself.
Obscure tables or unpublished drawings achieving 36 rectilinear crossings for K(5,7) could exist beyond retrieved queries; live search found no such witness but absence cannot be proved.

Heuristic search code was ephemeral and not part of certificate; reproducibility rests on witness plus verifiers, which is sufficient for the claim but does not explain why 36 is attainable structurally.
Single-witness result claims no uniqueness or minimal-coordinate property; future work may find simpler coordinates, which would not invalidate this certificate.
